title: introduce subword-aware tiler and circular-compact KV cache for FlashHybrid attention
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context and motivation: production workloads at varying tokenization granularities (BPE/subword mixes) were showing degraded kernel utilization and increased memory churn for medium-length sequences (96-512). Existing tiled FlashAttention paths assume uniform token alignment which produces suboptimal tiling and KV footprint for subword-heavy inputs. Additionally, small bursts cause frequent KV allocation/eviction churn that spikes p99 latency.

This PR introduces two complementary runtime changes to address these problems: (1) a subword-aware tiler for the FlashHybrid attention path which chooses tile boundaries aligned to tokenizer subword boundaries and sequence-chunk statistics, and (2) a circular-compact KV cache implementation that reduces fragmentation and lock contention during continuous batching. The net effect is improved throughput and lower p99 for mixed-length, subword-heavy workloads without changing models or prompts.

Summary of changes: 
- New runtime component: attn/subword_tiler.{cc,h} implementing a heuristic tiler that: computes a lightweight subword-alignment map from token metadata, biases tile sizes toward cache-friendly lengths (powers-of-two-like buckets), and emits tile descriptors consumed by the FlashHybrid scheduler.
- FlashHybrid attention: modified kernel launcher to accept tile descriptors and attempt a 'merge-pack' path that fuses QKV packing + apply_rotary into the tiler hotpath when rotary/rope is enabled. This reduces kernel launches for fused rotary and allows quant-friendly codepaths to stay contiguous.
- KV cache: added kv/circular_compact_cache.{cc,h} which manages a ring buffer of KV entries and supports in-place compaction when fragmentation exceeds a threshold. A background asynchronous compactor reduces eviction stalls for high-concurrency continuous batching.
- Scheduler: scheduler hints and a new 'tile_score' metric (empirically tuned) to prefer low-latency tile assignments for small interactive requests. The batching conductor now supports subtle prewarming when it detects repeated short sequences from the same client session.
- Tests & benchmarks: microbench harness updates under infra/perf/bench to measure median/p99 latency and throughput across sequence distributions with and without subword alignment metadata.

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests for subword tiler heuristics and corner cases (empty tokens, single-token sequences).
- [x] Integration test validating KV compaction correctness under concurrent writes.
- [x] Microbenchmarking harness for 8/16/32/64 GPU configs.
- [x] Backwards-compatible: existing callers that don't pass subword metadata are handled by a fallback tiler that mirrors previous behavior.

Performance summary (representative): 
- Mixed-length web-chat workload (tokenization: 35% subword-heavy messages): throughput +18% on A100 40GB, median latency -10%, p99 latency -22%.
- Short-interactive workload (<=64 tokens): p50 latency -12%, p99 -15% after prewarm warmup window.
- Memory: average KV footprint reduced by ~9% due to compaction and better tile packing (worst-case slight increase during async compaction spikes, but transient).

Compatibility & migration notes: 
- New API: internal runtime structure accepts optional per-request token_metadata[] (subword boundaries). Callers without this field see no change. The Redwood public API is unchanged.
- Rolling deploy: both tilers live side-by-side under feature flag runtime.experimental.subword_tiler. Flag default enabled for canary clusters.

How to test locally: 
1) run infra/perf/bench/subword_tiler_bench.py --config=local --gpus=1 to reproduce microbench harness.
2) unit tests: bazel test //runtime/attn/... //runtime/kv/...
3) integration: scripts/ci/run_kv_compaction_sanity.sh (simulates 200 concurrent clients)

Related: ENG-1842 (subword tiling experiment), ENG-1899 (kv-eviction incidents), PRs: redwood/pr-70321 (microstrip attn prefetch) - conceptually related but this PR focuses on tiling + KV compaction rather than prefetch scheduling.

Small illustrative diff (hotpath):
- runtime/attn/flash_hybrid_launcher.cc: added merge-pack path to reduce QKV+rotary kernel launches
  - old: launch_pack(); launch_apply_rotary(); launch_attention();
  - new: launch_merge_pack_apply_rotary_and_attn(tile_desc);

Notes: contains conservative fallbacks and runtime flags to allow safe rollback if canary metrics regress.
